newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin has heavy cold, cancels meetings.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin has heavy cold, cancels meetings.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin has "a heavy cold" and a temperature and has cancelled several meetings planned for the coming days, the Kremlin said on Monday.
But Yeltsin's press secretary Sergei Yastrzhembsky told a Kremlin briefing the illness had no relation to the 65-year-old Kremlin leader's recent heart bypass surgery.
He also said preparations for Yeltsin's heavy international schedule were going ahead "full swing".

This included a summit of the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS), scheduled for January 17 in Moscow, and a meeting with French President Jacques Chirac on February 2 at a country residence near Moscow.
Yeltsin is also due to travel to the Hague on February 4 to meet the current European Union president, Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok.

Yastrzhembsky said Yeltsin had held two meetings on Monday -- one on relations with NATO and a separate one with Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin -- "despite a heavy cold and temperature" of 37.5 degrees Celsius (99.5 Fahrenheit) in the morning."
"In this connection a number of meetings scheduled for the coming days have been postponed," Yastrzhembsky said. He gave no details and did not make clear if Yeltsin was still in his Kremlin office.
RIA news agency said a council of doctors, including the head of the Kremlin medical centre, Sergei Mironov, was meeting at Yeltsin's country residence to review the president's cold.
Yeltsin had a quintuple heart bypass operation on November 5 and returned to work at the end of last year.
